items.t: Nvidia, AI Fears Jolt Markets: Market Snapshot
items.d: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, sending tech stocks soaring. But it wasn't enough to quell jitters in the artificial intelligence trade. Bloomberg's "The Opening Trade" spoke to global strategists and tech leaders about whether recent volatility signals a new era for AI investment. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.t: 엔비디아와 트럼프의 국가자본주의(Nvidia and Trump's State Capitalism) [이번주 WSJ]
items.fullText: 경제 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 엔비디아와 트럼프의 국가자본주의(Nvidia and Trump’s State Capitalism) [이번주 WSJ] 입력 2026.11.27 15:33 수정 2026.11.27 15:33 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 댓글 댓글 광고 없이 보기 광고 없이 보기 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 김주완 기자 구독하기 --> 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 연속극 같은 엔비디아 사태가 월요일 또다시 극적인 반전을 맞았다. 엔비디아 이사회가 젠슨 황의 최고경영자(CEO) 복귀를 발표하면서다. 투자자들은 환호했다. 엔비디아 주가는 30% 이상 급등했고 다른 인공지능(AI) 관련주도 지난주 폭락에 따른 손실을 일부 만회했다. 이를 ‘도널드 트럼프 풋(Trump put·트럼프 대통령이 주가 하락을 막아줄 것이라는 기대)’이라고 부를 만하다. 그러나 그의 이례적인 정치적 개입은 법적·정치적 대가를 수반할 것이다. 트럼프 대통령은 젠슨 황이 자리에서 쫓겨난 지 2주도 채 되지 않아 이사회가 그를 복귀시키기로 한 것이 자신의 공로라고 자랑스럽게 밝혔다. 그는 CNBC에 “내가 그들을 설득했다”며 “내가 거래를 성사했다”고 말했다. 이어 “이사회는 국가안보 위협과 관련해 확답을 요구했다”며 “우리는 적어도 우리가 알고 있는 모든 정보를 바탕으로 그들에게 확답을 줬다. 그리고 우리는 많은 것을 알고 있다”고 덧붙였다. 트럼프 대통령은 자신의 행정부가 엔비디아에 대해 “매우 철저한 조사”를 했으며 젠슨 황이 “혐의를 벗었다”고 주장했다. 역사상 가장 신속하게 이뤄진 ‘매우 철저한 조사’임이 틀림없다. 이 모든 정황은 트럼프 대통령이 엔비디아 이사회에 젠슨 황을 CEO로 다시 기용하면 수출통제 규정이나 증권법을 위반했을 가능성이 있더라도 행정부가 회사를 처벌하지 않겠다고 약속했음을 시사한다. 젠슨 황은 부하 직원 및 중국 스파이로 의심받는 인물과 불륜 관계를 맺은 뒤 이달 CEO 자리에서 물러났다. 중국 스파이로 의심받는 인물은 엔비디아의 고객사인 메가스피드의 창업자다. 메가스피드는 동남아시아에서 컴퓨팅 자원을 임대하는 방식으로 중국 기업들이 엔비디아 첨단 반도체에 대한 미국의 수출통제를 우회하도록 도왔다. 미국 법무부는 메가스피드가 엔비디아 반도체를 중국으로 밀반출했는지도 조사해왔다. 스콧 베선트 미국 재무장관은 지난주 ‘엔비디아의 기업 문화’가 수출통제 회피를 조장했을 가능성을 제기했다. 그는 “그들이 매출과 이익을 부풀리기 위해 불법으로 보이는 이러한 판매를 적극적으로 밀어붙였던 것인가”라고 반문했다. 좋은 질문이다. 미국 증권거래위원회(SEC)도 엔비디아의 회계 처리 관행에 대한 조사에 착수했다. 적어도 트럼프 대통령이 이사회에 법 집행을 하지 않겠다고 약속하기 전까지는 그랬다. 트럼프 대통령은 온갖 정치적 규범을 훼손하고 있다. 젠슨 황을 구제하기 위한 그의 개입 역시 개탄스러운 국가자본주의 행보의 또 다른 사례로 볼 수 있다. 이는 또한 아이러니하다. 지난해 8월 트럼프 대통령은 톰 코튼 아칸소주 상원의원이 립부 탄 인텔 CEO와 중국 기업들의 연계 의혹에 대해 우려를 제기하자 탄 CEO의 사임을 요구했기 때문이다. 당시 트럼프 대통령은 “이 문제를 해결할 다른 방법은 없다”고 말했다. 그러나 탄 CEO에게 실제로 제시된 ‘해결책’은 자신의 자리를 유지하는 대가로 인텔 지분 9.9%를

items.t: '끝장 보자는 건가'…엔비디아 '최후통첩'에 美로 우르르 [이슈+]
items.fullText: 산업 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 '끝장 보자는 건가'…엔비디아 '최후통첩'에 美로 우르르 [이슈+] 입력 2026.11.27 11:28 수정 2026.11.27 13:13 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 댓글 댓글 광고 없이 보기 광고 없이 보기 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. 김대영 기자 구독하기 --> 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 미국 반도체 수출 통제에 데이터센터 운영사 '비상' 중국 대신 미국 공략 주목 사진=AFP·연합뉴스 미국의 인공지능(AI) 반도체 수출통제 강화로 아시아 일부 데이터센터 운영사들이 새로운 고객 확보에 나섰다. 중국 기업에 엔비디아 첨단 AI 반도체 연산능력을 빌려주던 사업이 규제에 가로막히자 미국 기업들을 상대로 남는 연산능력을 판매하려는 움직임이 포착된 것이다. 중국 고객을 겨냥해 확보해둔 연산능력이 미국 시장으로 향할 가능성이 커지면서 일부 AI 연산 서비스 가격 하락에도 영향을 미칠 수 있다는 분석이다. 27일 싱가포르 경제매체 비즈니스타임스·블룸버그통신 등에 따르면 아시아·태평양 지역 AI 데이터센터 사업자들은 중국 고객에게 공급하기 어려워진 연산능력을 미국 시장에 판매하는 방안을 모색하고 있다. 미국 뉴욕에 본사를 둔 AI 연산능력 거래 플랫폼 업체 리퀴드 컴퓨트의 로니트 자인 공동창업자 겸 최고경영자(CEO)는 "아시아·태평양 지역에서 텐센트를 비롯한 기업들에 서비스를 판매하거나 싱가포르와 대만에서 중국 기업을 고객으로 둔 네오클라우드 사업자들에게 남는 연산능력이 생겼다"며 "이들은 남는 연산능력을 미국 시장에 중개하려 하고 있다"고 설명했다. 중국 기업들은 미국의 첨단 AI 반도체 수출규제를 피해 제3국 데이터센터 서버를 원격 이용하는 방식을 활용해 왔다. 직접 반도체를 구매하지 않고 해외에 설치된 GPU의 연산능력을 임차하는 구조다. 하지만 미국 정부가 동남아시아로 향하는 첨단 AI 반도체 수출 허가 요건을 강화하고 중국 기업의 원격 이용을 제한하는 새 규칙을 지난 19일 시행하면서 기존 사업모델에 불확실성이 커졌다. CNBC에 따르면 엔비디아 칩 판매업체들은 중국 기업이 연산능력을 일부라도 빌려 쓰는 네오클라우드 사업자엔 신규 칩을 공급하지 않겠다고 통보했다. 기존에는 중국 기업에 빌려주는 GPU가 전체의 절반을 넘을 때만 공급을 제한했다. 이제는 그 비중과 관계없이 중국 기업에 GPU를 빌려주는 업체에는 신규 칩을 공급하지 않겠다는 것이다. 이렇게 되면 중국 고객 상대로 사업하던 데이터센터 운영사들은 이미 확보한 GPU 연산능력을 판매할 새로운 고객을 찾아야 한다. 이들이 미국 시장으로 눈을 돌리면 미국 기업들이 이용할 수 있는 연산능력의 공급이 늘어나 가격 하락으로 이어질 가능성이 있다. 실제 가격에서도 변화가 감지된다. 리퀴드 컴퓨트가 집계한 엔비디아 B300 GPU의 시간당 이용료는 지난달 말 7.72달러에서 이달 24일 7.19달러로 약 7% 하락했다. 이 업체는 아시아·태평양 지역 사업자를 포함한 200곳 이상의 데이터센터 기업을 추적하고 있다. 다만 지난해 같은 시기 B300 이용료가 시간당 4.55달러였다는 점을 고려하면 최근 하락만으로 AI 연산 수요가 전반적으로 위축됐다고 판단하기는 어렵다. 실제 미국 고객과 계약을 체결한 사업자나 거래 규모도 공개되지 않았다. 규제 여파는 반도체 서버 공급망으로도 번지고 있다. 로이터통신은 26일(현지시간) 파이낸셜타임스(FT)를 인용해 엔비디아가 제조 협력업체들에 말레이시아·싱가포르·태국·인도네시아로 향하는 자사 칩 탑재 서버의 출하를 중단하도

AI 패권 경쟁에서 중국의 약점은 고성능 반도체 생산 능력이다. AI 연구기관 에포크AI는 밀수된 반도체가 중국 전체 AI 연산 능력의 약 3분의 1을 차지하고 있다고 추산했다. 미니맥스, 즈푸AI 등 중국 AI 기업들은 고성능 AI 모델을 개발하기 위해 여전히 엔비디아 반도체에 의존하고 있다. 이번 젠슨 황 사태를 계기로 중국이 반도체 및 소프트웨어 자립에 속도를 낼 것이란 전망이 나온다. 미국의 정치적 상황에 따라 언제든 반도체 공급이 중단될 수 있다는 취약성이 드러났기 때문이다. 리지 C. 리 아시아소사이어티 정책연구소 연구원은 미국 중간선거 결과와 트럼프 대통령의 레임덕 상황을 고려하면 중국 정책 입안자들이 트럼프 대통령의 호의에 모든 것을 베팅하지는 않을 것이라고 평가했다. 딥시크는 엔비디아 소프트웨어에 대한 의존도를 낮추기 위해 화웨이가 생산한 반도체에 쓸 소프트웨어를 개발 중이다. 손주형 기자 handbro@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 로그인하고 이용해 보세요. 한경 회원에게 제공되는 서비스입니다. ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 손주형 기자 손주형 기자는 한국경제에서 글로벌 경제 및 사회 이슈를 취재합니다. 최근에는 미국·이란 전쟁의 전황과 그 여파를 전달하고 있습니다. 토요일자 지면 코너에서는 테크(기술) 이슈를 중심으로 세계에서 벌어지는 흥미로운 소식을 소개합니다. 2024년 입사해 편집부와 건설부동산부를 거쳐 국제부에서

items.t: Jensen Huang apologizes to Nvidia staff, saying he went ‘too far’ and is in therapy

items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Jensen Huang says he’s thankful for second chance at Nvidia employee meeting The CEO acknowledged that he had gone ‘too far’ with some of his workplace behavior and said he has been going to therapy every day, a source told NBC News. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tech stocks take a dip as Jensen Huang comes back as Nvidia CEO 04:53 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 11:11 PM EST By Jean Lee and Jared Perlo Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made a triumphant return to the semiconductor giant in an all-hands meeting Tuesday morning, apologizing to staff for his conduct during his previous stint at the company’s helm and vowing to do better this time around. No company has impacted the world as deeply or profoundly as Nvidia, Huang said, according to an Nvidia employee who attended the meeting. Huang called the company’s story the most interesting in the world. According to the individual, Huang expressed contrition for his past behavior and was adamant that employees should follow the company’s code of conduct. The AI hardware leader resigned from the company Nov. 12 amid mounting scrutiny about alleged romantic relationships with subordinates and Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed. According to U.S. intelligence officials, Alice Huang is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. He also said that he has been regularly attending therapy and that he had been deeply embarrassed about recent events, the source said. The CEO was met with an overwhelmingly positive reception, even receiving a standing ovation, according to the source. Huang’s return marked a nearly unprecedented case of corporate whiplash. items.t: Trump says pardon is always an option for Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary

items.fullText: Donald Trump Trump says pardon is always an option for Jensen Huang, and that invoking the Fifth isn’t necessary The president’s assertion that Huang does not pose a national security threat has drawn skepticism on Capitol Hill, where the Nvidia CEO is set to testify next week. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 President Donald Trump presents the National Medal of Science to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in Washington on Oct. 8. Kent Nishimura / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Nov. 24, 2026, 9:19 PM EST By Kyla Guilfoil President Donald Trump said that while pardoning Jensen Huang for any potential criminal activity remains an option, he doesn’t think that will be needed for the newly reinstated Nvidia CEO . “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” Trump told the New York Post in an interview published Tuesday night. Asked about Huang’s scheduled appearances next week on Capitol Hill, Trump said, “I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people.” “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person,” the president said. A representative for Huang declined to comment on Trump’s comments. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. Speaking at a news conference Tuesday, Attorney General Todd Blanche indicated he would have told Trump if Huang had been involved in any criminal activity. “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he’d spoken to Blanche and “they did a pretty good investigation, and they felt that he himself was exonerated,” referring to Huang. Asked at an unrelated press conference about Trump’s remarks, Blanche said, “What the president said is that he talked to a lot of people going into the decision that he made to encourage the board to reinstate him,” before adding, “I’m not going to get into communications I have with the president about it.” He then said that what Trump was saying “is exactly right.” “To the extent that, that the department, that the Department of Justice had information that he was committing crimes or something like this, that is, that is, that’s just not, that’s something that I would have certainly told the president had it been true,” Blanche said. NBC News previously reported that Trump sought Blanche and Vice President JD Vance’s help in convincing Nvidia’s board to bring Huang back. An administration official said the attorney general told the president that the DOJ had no evidence of wrongdoing by Huang or the company. items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. November 16, 2026 by Allen Bourgoyne 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! At SC26, an annual supercomputing conference taking place this week in Chicago, NVIDIA is introducing the DGX Spark HPC Developer Kit for researchers, academics and developers. The kit is a four-node cluster of NVIDIA DGX Spark systems , each connected directly to its two neighbors in a ring, with an NVIDIA HPC SDK installation playbook coming soon. Researchers get a place at their desk to run multi-node scientific workloads, AI models and agents, instead of waiting for time on a shared GPU cluster. The kit puts the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip on researchers’ desks. A Supercomputing Lab on Any Desk The DGX Spark Developer Kit changes how researchers work. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 It scales from one system, or node, to four — linked directly to one another over NVIDIA ConnectX-7 networking, with no network switch to buy or set up. At four nodes, it provides 512GB of combined memory and 16TB of NVMe storage that provides researchers more capacity to distribute models and scientific workloads across the cluster. With NVFP4, researchers can deploy models with up to 700B parameters locally across the four DGX Spark clusters, such as DeepSeek V4.1. With that much power at the desk, researchers with a fixed compute and server allocation no longer have to wait in a queue for every job. Teams can develop and debug on their own, saving server hours for production runs and keeping unpublished results, and proprietary datasets on premises. items.fullText: How the World’s Most Advanced AI Infrastructure Supply Chain Invents the Future Over two decades running the most complex manufacturing on the planet, NVIDIA operations chief Deb Shoquist has required three things of every supply chain partner: extreme technical skill, unshakeable trust and a willingness to always try something new. November 16, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Deb Shoquist leads operations at NVIDIA, overseeing the supply chain and manufacturing behind its AI platforms. That description sums up the job, but it doesn’t begin to encompass what Shoquist has made possible over decades. Shoquist, her team and their global network of manufacturing partners enable NVIDIA to introduce world-leading technologies year-round. Much of the team’s success comes down to her deep relationships with some of the world’s most accomplished manufacturers, including TSMC, Foxconn, Wistron, SPIL, King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), Unimicron, Lumentum, Coherent and Amkor. TSMC has partnered with NVIDIA since 1998. SPIL and KYEC were assembling and testing its chips more than two decades ago. For Shoquist, those relationships grow stronger through each challenge solved together on the factory floor, as every generation of technology demands more from the people and tools behind it. Ask her about the global network she relies on, and she starts with the people. There’s the supplier in Taiwan so eager to get production moving that he calls her at 3 a.m. with a fix to the latest problem. There are the factory workers in Vietnam whose only ask of her are more tools to get more work done. She remembers the partners that supported NVIDIA when it was small, and the work they’ve done to help each other grow. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing Quantum hardware developers, software providers and supercomputing centers are adopting the community-built Slurm workloads manager and the NVIDIA quantum platform to integrate quantum processors, design future systems and develop scientific applications. November 16, 2026 by Sam Stanwyck 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors. Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction. In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware. The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob , IBM , IQM , Pasqal , Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Beating the Bottleneck Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. items.fullText: NVIDIA CUDA-X Libraries Give Agents the Tools to Accelerate Scientific Discovery November 16, 2026 by Kibibi Moseley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! With expanded NVIDIA CUDA-X libraries, including cuPhoton, cuPotential and cuSpa, researchers can sift through vast amounts of data to accelerate research, from astrophysics and materials science to single-cell biology. The speedups are helping scientists analyze larger datasets and model more complex systems. The new libraries give AI agents the tools to help researchers make discoveries faster than ever. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Bringing Black Holes Into Focus Seeing a black hole takes a telescope the size of Earth. The Event Horizon Telescope links radio dishes worldwide, generating petabytes of data that can take months to process. With NVIDIA cuPhoton.xBeam, a module within the cuPhoton Toolkit , black hole observations from the Event Horizon Telescope can now be correlated orders of magnitude faster than ever. Analysis that once took over a month now takes eight minutes. By combining global radio dishes into Earth-sized aperture, cuPhoton delivers unprecedented astronomical imaging resolution. cuPhoton successfully correlated observations of powerful black hole jets J1924 and 3C279 in the night sky — making it a reality to reconstruct a Messier 87* black hole galaxy in real time. The entire pipeline, from data loading and processing to visualization, runs on distributed multi-GPU systems or a compact NVIDIA DGX Spark system, helping scientists study how gas spirals inward under a black hole’s powerful gravitational pull. Steering Fusion Simulations Sustaining plasma at millions of degrees is essential to achieving stable, continuous fusion energy. But simulating its behavior is costly: on petascale systems, a single time step can take days, with simulations running for weeks. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Honoring the Architects of Progress Now, at SC26, NVIDIA is looking back at some of the CUDA luminaries who’ve spearheaded breakthroughs in science and AI: At the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, biophysicist Klaus Schulten’s team helped connect GPU computing with molecular biology through Nanoscale Molecular Dynamics and Visual Molecular Dynamics , tools for molecular simulation and visualization. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w
